intro: Covariance and least-squares calculations often involve symmetric positive definite matrices. A triangular square root exposes their structure.
task: Compute the lower-triangular Cholesky factor with positive diagonal using the column recurrence.
requirements: matrix is square and symmetric within absolute tolerance 1e-10.
Return lower-triangular L satisfying L@L.T=matrix. At each diagonal, subtract previously accumulated squares before taking the positive square root.
Reject a computed diagonal pivot at or below 1e-12. Semidefinite matrices are outside this positive-definite exercise.

Use real finite numeric inputs with magnitude at most 1e6, excluding booleans. Vectors have length 1..128 and matrix axes have length 1..128 unless a tighter bound is stated. Leave all inputs unchanged; raise ValueError for invalid inputs.

examples.name: Single entry

hints.title: Find the structure
hints.body: Earlier factor columns already explain part of each matrix entry; subtract their inner product first.

hints.title: Build the calculation
hints.body: Diagonal residuals are squared factor entries, while off-diagonal residuals divide by an already known diagonal.

explanation: At position (i,j), earlier factor columns already explain part of the original matrix entry. Subtracting that contribution leaves the next diagonal square or off-diagonal product.
A positive pivot is essential. A zero or negative residual cannot be represented by a real positive diagonal factor under this contract.
